  1000	// dashLayout is the computed column geometry for one render pass. Computed
  1001	// once per View() from m.width + the current items so every renderer sees the
  1002	// same dimensions. termWidth=0 (before the first WindowSizeMsg) is handled by
  1003	// falling back to an 80-col baseline in computeLayout.
  1004	type dashLayout struct {
  1005		mode         layoutMode
  1006		termWidth    int
  1007		contentWidth int // total visible row width, including the leading "  " indent
  1008		nameWidth    int
  1009		branchWidth  int
  1010		ageWidth     int
  1011		dirtyWidth   int
  1012		syncWidth    int
  1013		prWidth      int
  1014		reviewWidth  int
  1015		ciWidth      int
  1016		statusWidth  int // used only when mode == layoutNarrow

  1019	// tailWidth is the width of the trailing PR/Review/CI cluster (full mode) or
  1020	// the Status cell (narrow mode). Used by per-row overlays (prune, rebase) so
  1021	// they fill the same horizontal slot.
  1022	func (l dashLayout) tailWidth() int {
  1023		if l.mode == layoutNarrow {
  1024			return l.statusWidth
  1025		}

  1030	// "  " margin and the row's right edge. Used for dividers and for aligning

  1038	// minNarrowWidth returns the smallest terminal width that fits the narrow
  1039	// layout for the given name column — used by the tiny-mode hint message.
  1040	func minNarrowWidth(nameWidth int) int {
  1041		// "  " + cursor(2) + current(2) + name + "  " + minBranch + " " + age + " "
  1042		// + dirty + " " + sync + " " + status
  1043		return 2 + 2 + 2 + nameWidth + 2 + colBranchMin + 1 + colAge + 1 + colDirty + 1 + colSync + 1 + colStatus
  1044	}
  1045	
  1046	// computeLayout chooses a mode and column widths for the given terminal size.
  1047	// Branch column flexes to consume any slack; PR/Review/CI collapse to a single
  1048	// Status column when there isn't enough room. termWidth <= 0 (initial render
  1049	// before WindowSizeMsg) falls back to 80 columns — a conservative default
  1050	// that fits in tmux, vsplit panes, and most "default" terminal sizes.
  1051	func computeLayout(items []DashItem, termWidth int) dashLayout {
  1052		nameWidth := 8
  1053		for _, it := range items {
  1054			nameWidth = max(nameWidth, lipgloss.Width(it.ShortName))
  1055		}
  1056	
  1057		if termWidth <= 0 {
  1058			termWidth = 80
  1059		}
  1060		avail := termWidth - 2 // leading "  " indent
  1061	
  1062		// Fixed widths excluding the branch column.
  1063		fixedFull := 2 + 2 + nameWidth + 2 + 1 + colAge + 1 + colDirty + 1 + colSync + 1 + (colPR + 1 + colReview + 1 + colCI)
  1064		fixedNarrow := 2 + 2 + nameWidth + 2 + 1 + colAge + 1 + colDirty + 1 + colSync + 1 + colStatus
  1065	
  1066		lo := dashLayout{
  1067			termWidth:   termWidth,
  1068			nameWidth:   nameWidth,
  1069			ageWidth:    colAge,
  1070			dirtyWidth:  colDirty,
  1071			syncWidth:   colSync,
  1072			prWidth:     colPR,
  1073			reviewWidth: colReview,
  1074			ciWidth:     colCI,
  1075			statusWidth: colStatus,
  1076		}
  1077	
  1078		switch {
  1079		case avail >= fixedFull+colBranchMin:
  1080			lo.mode = layoutFull
  1081			lo.branchWidth = clampInt(avail-fixedFull, colBranchMin, colBranchMax)
  1082			lo.contentWidth = 2 + fixedFull + lo.branchWidth // "  " + row content
  1083		case avail >= fixedNarrow+colBranchMin:
  1084			lo.mode = layoutNarrow
  1085			lo.branchWidth = clampInt(avail-fixedNarrow, colBranchMin, colBranchMax)
  1086			lo.contentWidth = 2 + fixedNarrow + lo.branchWidth
  1087		default:
  1088			lo.mode = layoutTiny
  1089		}
  1090		return lo
  1091	}

  1093	func clampInt(v, lo, hi int) int {
  1094		if v < lo {
  1095			return lo
  1096		}
  1097		if v > hi {
  1098			return hi
  1099		}
  1100		return v
  1101	}

  1103	// bodyLineCap returns how many PR body lines the detail panel may render.
  1104	// Caps at 6 in comfortable terminals; scales down on short ones so the body
  1105	// doesn't push commits/files off the bottom of the screen. The "-20" is a
  1106	// rough reservation for the table, sections, and footer — not exact, just
  1107	// predictable: 26-row terminals get the full 6 lines, 22 rows give 2, 20 or
  1108	// fewer drop the body entirely. termHeight=0 (before the first WindowSizeMsg)
  1109	// falls back to the ceiling.
  1110	func bodyLineCap(termHeight int) int {
  1111		const ceiling = 6
  1112		if termHeight <= 0 {
  1113			return ceiling
  1114		}
  1115		n := termHeight - 20
  1116		switch {
  1117		case n < 0:
  1118			return 0
  1119		case n > ceiling:
  1120			return ceiling
  1121		}
  1122		return n
  1123	}

  1167		if lo.mode == layoutFull {

  1190		// Rows

  1317	// footerKeys returns the footer key hints, one styled string per key.
  1318	// r/R/c get a struck-through look when the cursor row can't take them
  1319	// (busy, base branch, or current worktree).
  1320	func footerKeys(m dashModel) []string {
  1321		keys := worktreeKeyHelp
  1322		enabled := map[string]bool{}
  1323		rLabel := "rebase"
  1324		if m.focus == focusCommits {
  1325			keys = commitKeyHelp
  1326		} else {
  1327			// cursor out of range only happens when items is empty — treat
  1328			// actions as disabled then.
  1329			var cur DashItem
  1330			rowExists := m.cursor >= 0 && m.cursor < len(m.items)
  1331			if rowExists {
  1332				cur = m.items[m.cursor]
  1333			}
  1334			busy := rowExists && m.rowBusy(cur.Path)
  1335			enabled["s"] = rowExists
  1336			enabled["r"] = rowExists && !busy
  1337			enabled["R"] = m.countRebaseTargets() > 0
  1338			enabled["c"] = rowExists && canClose(cur) && !busy
  1339			// Base-branch rows fast-forward from the remote rather than rebase.
  1340			if rowExists && cur.IsBase {
  1341				rLabel = "fast-forward"
  1342			}
  1343		}

  1346		for _, k := range keys {
  1347			if !k.footer {

  1360		}

  1364	// layoutFooter wraps the key hints to width and puts status at the right
  1365	// edge of the last line, or on a line of its own when it doesn't fit.
  1366	func layoutFooter(parts []string, status string, width int) []string {
  1367		sep := dStyleDim.Render(" · ")
  1368		var lines []string

  1371			switch {
  1372			case line == "":

  1374			case lipgloss.Width(line)+lipgloss.Width(sep)+lipgloss.Width(p) <= width:
  1375				line += sep + p
  1376			default:
  1377				lines = append(lines, line)
  1378				line = p
  1379			}
  1380		}
  1381		if status != "" {
  1382			if pad := width - lipgloss.Width(line) - lipgloss.Width(status); pad >= 2 {
  1383				line += strings.Repeat(" ", pad) + status
  1384			} else {
  1385				lines = append(lines, line)
  1386				line = status
  1387			}
  1388		}
  1389		return append(lines, line)
  1390	}

  1423	func (m dashModel) renderRow(it DashItem, isCursor bool, lo dashLayout) string {

  1444

  1446		// Recent commits get a green tint so fresh worktrees pop. Stale rows always

  1461	
  1462		// Tail cluster: PR/Review/CI in full mode, single Status cell in narrow mode.

  1464		// with the column header above.

  1481			ageRendered, dirty, syncRendered, tail,
  1482		)

  1486			// the inner foreground colors and just add a background.

content.text:
I found and fixed eight real bugs, one of which lost data, plus a batch of smaller cleanups. Nothing is committed. Tests, vet and lint pass, and I reproduced the first six bugs in a scratch repo before fixing them, then confirmed each fix there.

## Fixed

**Bugs**
- **`wt move` deleted files.** Any changed file with a space or non-ASCII character in its name was dropped from the source and never copied. Git quotes such paths unless asked not to, so the status parser now uses `-z`.
- **`wt switch -` never worked across worktrees.** The previous-worktree marker was written to one worktree's git dir and read from another's. It now lives in the shared git dir.
- **`wt rebase --all` moved `main` to the base branch.** With `base_branch = "staging"`, a worktree on `main` was fast-forwarded to `origin/staging`. The dashboard's fast-forward had the same fault.
- **`wt close` and `wt rename` failed from a subdirectory.** Both treated the current directory as the worktree root.
- **`wt switch feat` could cd into a plain directory.** With a `feat/foo` worktree, `feat` matched as an exact hit. Matching now uses the worktree list, and `foo` resolves to `feat/foo` without the fuzzy warning.
- **`wt prune` could remove a worktree with an open PR.** A reused branch name with an old merged or closed PR counted as stale.
- **`wt init` made copied files world-readable.** A `0600` `.env` came out `0644`.
- **Bare `wt` never showed review or CI status.** It fetched only the PR number, so those lines were dead.

**Smaller fixes**
- Dashboard diff stats counted the base branch's new commits as deletions, and paths with spaces were cut short.
- A long commit subject in the dashboard could be cut inside a colour code.
- `wt watch <branch>` now works for branches that aren't checked out, as its help says.
- `wt list --output <unknown>` now errors instead of printing the table.
- Bun's text lockfile `bun.lock` is detected.
- The dashboard's conflict message no longer suggests `--continue` after it has aborted the rebase.

**Efficiency and dead code**
- Every command ran `git worktree list` three times at startup; now once.
- Ahead/behind takes one git call instead of two.
- Removed four unused functions and two duplicated helpers.

**Docs**
- README, the root help and the Homebrew caveat still said `wt new` changes directory. It stopped doing that in commit `28edd43`.
- Corrected stale comments and `wt switch` help, and updated `CLAUDE.md`.

## For you to review

- **Unpushed check has a hole.** A branch with no upstream counts as zero unpushed commits, so `wt close` and the dashboard's `c` delete it without asking. Default git config sets an upstream on `wt new`, so this only hits users with `branch.autoSetupMerge=false`.
- **`wt prune` ignores unpushed commits.** It checks only for uncommitted changes before force-deleting the branch.
- **Hooks are skipped by `wt prune` and the dashboard close.** Only `wt close` runs `pre_close` and `post_close`.
- **`wt rename` recreates the PR**, which loses reviews and comments. GitHub's branch-rename API keeps the PR.
- **`wt open` can't open merged or closed PRs**, and its "PR is closed" warning can never fire.

# Rex

Manage sessions, arrange panes, and run commands with the Rex command-line tool.

## Overview

Run the installed `rex` command directly. It locates and connects to the Rex
server automatically. Use the CLI's built-in commands to manage Rex without
scripting the app's interface or communicating with the server's socket directly.

## Identify your session and pane

Rex sets two environment variables when it opens a terminal. The context provided
at the start of your session includes their values:

- `REX_SESSION` identifies your session. Pass `-s "$REX_SESSION"` to select it
  for a command.
- `REX_BLOCK` identifies your terminal pane. Pass `-b "$REX_BLOCK"` to select
  that pane, for example when creating a split beside it.

These values identify where you're running. The user may be viewing a different
session or pane. Choose the target based on the request:

- **"Here", "beside you", or no location at all.** Use `$REX_SESSION` and
  `$REX_BLOCK`.
- **"The focused pane" or "the current tab".** Inspect the session the user is
  viewing with `rex session inspect SESSION --json`. In `windows`, find the
  window whose `window_id` matches `active_window_id`. Use that window's
  `focused_block_id` to select its focused pane.
- **A session, tab, or pane by name.** Find the named target in a listing. An
  explicit target takes precedence over your location or the app's focus.

If `REX_SESSION` isn't set, run `rex whoami --json` to check your connection, then
`rex ls --json` to list the available sessions. Use the session that matches the
request. Ask the user to choose if more than one session matches.

The startup context contains inherited IDs without checking whether they are
still available. If a target can't be found, run `rex whoami --json` to check
your current connection and location. It reports only IDs that exist on the
connected server.

Several versions of Rex may be running at once. Don't terminate Rex processes
or restart the server unless the user asks.

Inspect the state you need for the task:

```sh
rex window ls -s "$REX_SESSION" --json
rex block ls -s "$REX_SESSION" --json
rex session inspect "$REX_SESSION" --json
```

`session inspect` reports `active_window_id` and the layout of every window in
`windows`. Each window includes its `window_id` and `focused_block_id`.
`rex block inspect` reports the block's window ID in `.block.window_id` and lists
the methods available on the block. Use full IDs in later commands to avoid
ambiguity. Labels and ID suffixes may match more than one resource.

## Name the session

Rename the session only when the user asks, using the label they give or one
that names the task:

```sh
rex session rename "$REX_SESSION" 'fix-login-redirect'
```

## Use Rex terminology

| User term or request | Rex term or command |
| --- | --- |
| Session, workspace | A session: `rex new NAME` |
| Tab | A window in a session: `rex window new -s SESSION NAME` |
| Pane, terminal | A block in a window |
| Open a command in a new tab | `rex run -s SESSION -- COMMAND...` |
| Open a named tab with a command | `rex window new -s SESSION NAME -- COMMAND...` |
| Split beside a pane | `rex split -s SESSION -b BLOCK --split=right -- COMMAND...` |
| Read a terminal's output | `rex capture -s SESSION -b BLOCK --trim` |
| Type text, press a key | `rex send`, `rex send-key` |
| Maximize a pane, restore the layout | `rex zoom BLOCK --on`, `--off` |
| Rex app on a particular Mac or device | A client: `rex client ls` |
| Show a session in the app | `rex -C CLIENT do session.select session_id=SESSION` |

In the CLI, a window is a tab within a session. `rex new` creates a session with
one terminal tab. The command doesn't ask an app to display the new session.
To display a session in the app, use a client action, as described in
[Control Rex apps](#control-rex-apps).

## Build commands

- **Put Rex options before `--` and the command to run after it.** Pass the
  command and its arguments as separate words. Use `-- sh -c 'cmd1 | cmd2'` when
  the command needs shell syntax, such as a pipe. By default, Rex uses the login
  shell's environment. Pass `--shell=none` to run the program directly.
- **Set the working directory with `-c "$project_dir"`** when it matters. On a
  remote server, use paths and programs available on the remote machine.
- **`run` opens a new tab** unless you pass `--split`. `split` places the new pane
  on the right by default. The directions for placing a pane are `right`,
  `left`, `above`, and `below`. The directions for moving focus are `left`,
  `right`, `up`, and `down`.
- **`--ratio 30` gives the new pane 30 percent of the split.** The option accepts
  values from 1 to 99. When building a layout in several steps, position each
  new pane relative to a block ID returned by an earlier command.
- **New panes and tabs take focus.** Pass `--focus=false` for background work, or
  when the user wants to keep the current focus.
- **Pass `--keep-open` for output the user should read** after the program exits.
  Use `run --wait` or `split --wait` when you need the exit status of a command
  that finishes. Omit `--wait` for editors, monitors, and development servers.
- **`run --label` labels the pane.** `window new NAME` names the tab.
- **Save the IDs each command returns.** `new --json` returns `.session_id` and
  `.initial_windows[0].block_ids`. `window new`, `run`, and `split --json` return
  `.block_ids` and include `.window_id` when they create a window. `split` also
  returns the original pane's ID. Use `.block_ids[0]` to select the new pane in
  later commands.
- **Check the result before retrying a command that timed out.** The command may
  have succeeded. Inspect the state to avoid creating duplicate tabs or sessions.

## Common requests

The following examples use `$REX_SESSION` and `$REX_BLOCK` for your session and
terminal. Set `project_dir` to the project's absolute path. If the current
directory is the project directory, use `project_dir="$PWD"`.

Variables such as `editor_block`, `logs_block`, and `tab_id` hold full IDs
returned by an earlier command or found in a listing. If separate shell calls
don't preserve variables, pass the values directly. The examples use `jq` to
read JSON output.

### Open a tab with a diff

Use the project's version control system. For a Jujutsu repository, identified
by a `.jj/` directory at its root, run:

```sh
rex window new -s "$REX_SESSION" Diff -c "$project_dir" --keep-open --json -- jj --no-pager diff
```

For a Git repository:

```sh
rex window new -s "$REX_SESSION" Diff -c "$project_dir" --keep-open --json -- git --no-pager diff
```

Both commands keep the diff visible after the command exits. `git diff` shows
unstaged changes to tracked files. For staged Git changes, use
`git --no-pager diff --cached`. If the user specifies revisions, include them
in the diff command. To open an interactive diff viewer, use `-- lazygit` when
it's installed. If the user requests a built-in viewer, check the block types
available on the connected server.

# /wt-release - Release a new wt version

Tag and release a new version of wt. GoReleaser builds binaries and updates the Homebrew formula automatically.

## Steps

1. Run `git status` in the wt project root (`~/Dev/wt`) — abort if there are uncommitted changes or if `main` differs from `origin/main`
2. Run `git log --oneline -5` to show recent commits
3. Check the latest git tag with `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` to determine the current version
4. Ask the user what the new version should be (suggest a patch bump, e.g. v1.22.1 → v1.22.2)
5. Check that CI passed on HEAD: `gh run list --branch main --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD) --limit 1` — wait with `gh run watch <id> --exit-status` if it's still running, and abort if it failed
6. Run `git tag <version> && git push origin <version>`
7. Watch the release run (`gh run list --workflow release.yml --limit 1`, then `gh run watch <id> --exit-status`) and report the result
8. Update the local install: `git -C $(brew --repository mvwi/homebrew-tap) pull origin main && brew reinstall wt`, then confirm with `wt --version`
